content.text:
I have inspected all responsive locations. Summary of the bargain:

- **Ownership (10.1(a), p0423)**: each Party's Third Parties assign Program Inventions to that Party; Sanofi Sole Program Know-How/Patents are defined as inventions "owned solely by Sanofi pursuant to Section 10.1(a)". No assignment of Sanofi IP to RevMed during the Term.
- **Joint IP (10.1(b), p0424)**: joint ownership exists, but each Party may exploit and license "without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent", plus an irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable cross-licence — i.e. joint ownership *with* an unrestricted right to exploit (not walk-away).
- **Vendor background IP (3.3, p0253)**: RevMed retains its background technology only — permitted.
- **Deliverable-type assignment to us (6.2, p0339)**: RevMed "hereby does assign, to Sanofi all of its rights, title and interests in and to all Regulatory Approvals".
- **Licence quality (3.1/3.4/12.3(b))**: exclusive, worldwide (Licensed Territory = all countries), sublicensable through multiple tiers, to exploit Products; and on expiry it becomes "fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable".
- **Vendor licence in our data/rights (3.2, p0252)**: limited "solely to the extent necessary for RevMed to perform its obligations under this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements" — service-delivery-limited, not independent exploitation.

input.quote: Upon expiration of this Agreement, the licenses granted to Sanofi under Section 3.1 will become fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable.
input.rationale: The IP package satisfies the fallback and most of the preferred position. RevMed retains only its pre-existing/background technology (3.3, p0253: "RevMed hereby retains ... all rights in and to the RevMed Licensed Technology other than the rights expressly licensed to Sanofi"), while Sanofi solely owns its own Program Inventions (1.109/1.110 keyed to Section 10.1(a)) and RevMed "hereby does assign, to Sanofi all of its rights, title and interests in and to all Regulatory Approvals" (6.2, p0339). Our licence under 3.1 is exclusive, covers all uses in the Licensed Territory (all countries of the world), is sublicensable through multiple tiers (3.4(b)), and becomes fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable on expiration (12.3(b), p0499) — meeting the perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free/use-modify-sublicense fallback elements; the royalty during the Term is the deal price, not an IP deviation. The only licence running to RevMed in our materials is the 3.2 grant-back, expressly limited "solely to the extent necessary for RevMed to perform its obligations under this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements", i.e. service delivery rather than independent exploitation. Noted but not redlined: joint ownership of Joint Program Technology departs from the preferred "no joint ownership" element, but 10.1(b) gives each Party an unrestricted right to exploit and license without accounting or consent, plus an irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable cross-licence for any and all purposes, so it is not walk-away territory. The post-termination transfer of Regulatory Approvals to RevMed (12.3(c)) is a customary reversion of terminated Products and is handled under the termination rule, not IP.
